title: Get a marriage license
question: How do we get a marriage license in Albemarle County?
office: Clerk of the Albemarle County Circuit Court (elected constitutional officer)
summary: Any Virginia circuit court clerk issues marriage licenses. In Albemarle it is the Circuit Court Clerk's Office at the courthouse on Court Square (350 Park Street, Charlottesville), open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm; call 434-972-4083 first. You can start the application online through the Clerk's linked program (albemarlemarriage.org), then swear to it before the clerk. State law sets the fee at $30: a $20 state tax plus a $10 clerk fee. Both people must be 18. Marry anywhere in Virginia within 60 days; the officiant returns the certificate to the Albemarle clerk within five days. An officiant who is not a minister or listed official needs a clerk's order ($25). Certified copies: from the clerk (fee not published) or from Vital Records ($15 a copy).

legal_basis.quote: Every marriage in this Commonwealth shall be under a license and solemnized in the manner herein provided.
Every license for a marriage shall be issued by the clerk or deputy clerk of a circuit court of any county or city.

If from any cause neither the clerk nor his deputy is able to issue the license, it may be issued by the judge of the circuit court of such county, or city, who shall make return thereof to the clerk as soon as there may be one.

No person authorized by § 20-14 to issue a marriage license shall deny the issuance of such license to two parties contemplating a lawful marriage on the basis of the sex, gender, or race of such parties.
Religious organizations and members of the clergy acting in their religious capacity shall have the right to refuse to perform any marriage.
The minimum age at which persons may marry shall be 18.
A marriage entered into prior to the dissolution of an earlier marriage of one of the parties;
A marriage between an ancestor and descendant, or between siblings, whether the relationship is by the half or the whole blood or by adoption;
A marriage between an uncle or aunt and a nephew or niece, whether the relationship is by the half or the whole blood.
The clerk issuing any marriage license shall require the parties contemplating marriage to state, under oath, the information required to complete the application for marriage license.
The parties shall be able to designate themselves on the application for marriage license as spouse, bride, or groom.

The clerk shall provide the parties with two copies of the marriage certificate to be completed by the marriage officiant, who shall return the completed certificates to the clerk after the marriage ceremony of the parties.

The clerk may provide the parties with a commemorative marriage certificate and the parties may request a certified copy of the official marriage certificate as provided in Article 7 (§ 32.1-270 et seq.) of Chapter 7 of Title 32.1.

The State Registrar shall furnish forms for the marriage license, marriage certificate, and application for marriage license used in the Commonwealth.
On each marriage license issued under § 20-14 there is hereby levied a license tax of $20, which tax shall be collected by the clerk when the license is issued
Ten dollars of this license tax shall be allocated to the Virginia Department of Social Services for the purpose of providing services to victims of domestic violence.

Every marriage license issued under § 20-14 shall constitute authority for a period of only sixty days from the date of issuance for the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees.
Whenever such sixty-day period shall have elapsed without the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees, the license shall expire.
no new license shall be issued except in compliance with all provisions of law applicable to the issuance of a license in the first instance.

Upon application filed with the clerk of the circuit court and payment of applicable clerk's fees, such clerk may issue an order authorizing one or more persons to celebrate the rites of marriage in the Commonwealth.
Any person so authorized may be required to, before acting, enter into bond in the penalty of $500, with or without surety, as the clerk may direct.
Any order made under this section may be rescinded at any time.
The clerk of any circuit court shall be immune from any cause of action that arises from the issuance or rescinding of an order under this section, absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.

For recording an order to celebrate the rites of marriage pursuant to § 20-25 , $25 to be paid by the petitioner.

the actual cost of the ceremony together with travel expenses shall be given to the parties at least three days prior to the marriage ceremony.

If any person knowingly perform the ceremony of marriage without lawful license, or officiate in celebrating the rites of marriage without being authorized by law to do so, he shall be confined in jail not exceeding one year, and fined not exceeding $500.

steps.step: Check that you can marry in Virginia
steps.who: Both people who plan to marry
steps.how: Both of you must be at least 18. Neither of you may still be married to someone else: an earlier marriage must be ended first. Virginia also bars marriage between an ancestor and a descendant, between siblings (half or whole blood, or by adoption), and between an uncle or aunt and a nephew or niece. The clerk may not refuse a license because of the couple's sex, gender or race. No Code section or Albemarle page requires you to live in Albemarle County or in Virginia: the law lets the clerk of any Virginia circuit court issue the license, and the Clerk's 2021 service notice said any circuit court clerk's office in Virginia can issue one for a marriage in Virginia.
steps.quote: The minimum age at which persons may marry shall be 18.

steps.step: Choose an authorized officiant and a wedding date no more than 60 days after you will get the license
steps.how: The ceremony must be performed in Virginia by someone the law authorizes. That can be a minister who holds an order from a circuit court, its judge or its clerk (Va. Code § 20-23); religious organizations and clergy acting in their religious capacity may refuse to perform any marriage (§ 20-13.2). It can be a judge, a circuit court clerk or another official listed in § 20-25, who needs no order or bond. Anyone else, such as a friend or relative, must first get a clerk's order under § 20-25 (step s3). A religious society with no ordained minister may marry its members by its own practice; one person the society chooses completes the certificate and must give a $500 bond with surety (§ 20-26). A person authorized under § 20-25 may charge no more than $75 for the ceremony, plus travel expenses, and must tell you the full cost at least three days before the ceremony. The Albemarle Clerk's pages list no officiants and offer no courthouse ceremonies; they post only the petition for a one-time ceremony (step s3). Do not get the license until the wedding is within 60 days.
steps.deadline: Plan the ceremony within 60 days of the date the license will be issued; an officiant authorized under § 20-25 must give you the cost at least three days before the ceremony
steps.fee: Officiant's fee, if any (no more than $75 per ceremony, plus travel, for a person authorized under § 20-25)
steps.quote: may celebrate the rites of marriage anywhere in the Commonwealth without the necessity of bond or order of authorization.

steps.step: If your officiant is not a minister or a listed official, the officiant applies to the Clerk for an order authorizing them to perform the marriage
steps.who: The officiant (applicant); Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office (its Civil Division page posts the older petition; its Forms link leads to the current CC-1498 on vacourts.gov)
steps.how: The officiant fills in and signs the state form CC-1498, Application for Authorization to Celebrate Rites of Marriage (Persons Other Than Ministers), and files it with the Clerk. The form asks for the officiant's name, home and mailing addresses and phone number. It asks for authority either for one marriage (the couple's names and the approximate date) or for continuing authority. The officiant may also ask that no bond be required. The officiant pays $25 to record the order, and the clerk may require a $500 bond, with or without surety. The Albemarle Clerk's Office does not require its civil cover page for this request. The Clerk's Civil Division page and Documents Center ('Perform Marriage Ceremony - Updated') still link an older two-page 2018 version (a petition to the Court with an order for a judge's signature). The Clerk's 'Forms for Various Circuit Court Filings' link goes to the vacourts.gov civil forms page, which has the current July 2026 version and its instructions ('submitted to the Clerk of the Circuit Court'). Ask the Clerk's Office which one it accepts and how long it takes. An order can be rescinded at any time.
steps.fee: $25 to record the order (paid by the petitioner); a $500 bond, with or without surety, only if the clerk requires one

steps.step: Start the marriage license application online (the Clerk's automated application program)
steps.how: The Clerk's Office page links 'Marriage License Application' to albemarlemarriage.org, the Clerk's automated marriage license application program. Enter your information as accurately as you can. The welcome page does not say what the application asks, whether it is required, or what you do after submitting it, and lexflow did not open the application itself. State law still requires you to swear to the information before the clerk (step s6). Questions go to the Clerk's Office at (434) 972-4083.
steps.quote: Please complete your application ensuring that all information is as accurate as possible.

steps.step: Gather the information and identification you will need
steps.how: State law requires each of you to give the information on the state application form under oath. Each of you must include your social security number, or a control number issued by the DMV, and sign the application. You may list yourselves as spouse, bride or groom. The Albemarle Clerk's pages give no list of required documents. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID; other Virginia clerks ask for one, but Albemarle's requirement is not published. If either of you was married before, know when and how that marriage ended. No Virginia Code section requiring a blood test or a copy of a divorce decree was found.
steps.quote: The parties shall also include their social security numbers or other control numbers issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles pursuant to § 46.2-342 and affix their signatures to the application for such license.

steps.step: Go to the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office and swear to the application
steps.who: Both people (plan for both to attend; see caveats); the clerk or a deputy clerk
steps.how: Go to the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office, Albemarle County Courthouse, Court Square, 350 Park Street, Charlottesville, during Clerk's Office hours, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. In June 2025 the Circuit Court and its Clerk's Office moved into the new courthouse adjacent to Court Square; the County and court pages still give 350 Park Street, so confirm the entrance. Call (434) 972-4083 first to ask whether you need an appointment and whether both of you must come. The clerk has you state the application information under oath; a false statement can be prosecuted as perjury. Expect security screening: the Sheriff's Office says everyone entering the courts is subject to search. It also bars cell phones and other electronic or recording devices beyond the security screening desks at the Circuit Court.
steps.deadline: Clerk's Office hours, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm
steps.quote: The clerk issuing any marriage license shall require the parties contemplating marriage to state, under oath, the information required to complete the application for marriage license.

steps.step: Pay the license fee and receive the license and two copies of the marriage certificate
steps.how: State law sets the fee at $30. That is the $20 state license tax, of which $10 funds services for victims of domestic violence, plus the clerk's $10 fee for issuing the license, the oaths, and indexing and recording. The Albemarle Clerk's pages do not state the amount charged or the payment methods accepted, so ask when you call. The clerk gives you the license and two copies of the marriage certificate for your officiant to complete. No Virginia Code section setting a waiting period was found; the 60 days run from the date of issuance (§ 20-14.1).
steps.fee: $30 under state law ($20 state license tax plus $10 clerk's fee); Albemarle's own amount and payment methods are not published
steps.quote: On each marriage license issued under § 20-14 there is hereby levied a license tax of $20, which tax shall be collected by the clerk when the license is issued

steps.step: Hold the ceremony anywhere in Virginia within 60 days
steps.how: The license authorizes a ceremony in Virginia for 60 days from the date it is issued. If 60 days pass without a ceremony, it expires, and you must apply again: a new license must meet every requirement for a first license, and the fee is charged again. Anyone who knowingly performs a ceremony without a lawful license, or officiates without legal authority, can be jailed for up to a year and fined up to $500 (§ 20-28). A marriage under a Virginia license is not void just because the officiant lacked authority or the license had a defect, if the marriage is otherwise lawful and either or both spouses fully believed they were lawfully married (§ 20-31).
steps.deadline: Within 60 days from the date of issuance
steps.quote: Every marriage license issued under § 20-14 shall constitute authority for a period of only sixty days from the date of issuance for the solemnization of a marriage of the licensees.

steps.step: The officiant completes the certificate and returns it to the Albemarle Clerk within five days
steps.who: The officiant; the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: After the ceremony the officiant certifies the facts of the marriage and files the record, in duplicate, with the clerk who issued the license (here the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk). This must be done within five days. The clerk files and indexes the original in the marriage register. By the tenth day of the next month, the clerk sends the state's copy to the State Registrar of Vital Records. A minister (§ 20-23) or other authorized person (§ 20-25) who does not comply faces a $25 penalty (§ 20-24). By March 31 each year the clerk lists the previous year's unreturned licenses for the Albemarle Commonwealth's Attorney.
steps.deadline: Within five days after the ceremony
steps.quote: Every person who officiates at a marriage ceremony shall certify to the facts of marriage and file the record in duplicate with the officer who issued the marriage license within five days after the ceremony.

steps.step: Get certified copies of the marriage certificate
steps.who: Either spouse (or another person entitled to the record); the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office, the Virginia Department of Health Office of Vital Records, or the DMV
steps.how: The Albemarle Clerk keeps the original and can certify copies; call (434) 972-4083 to ask how to request one and what it costs. The Clerk's pages publish no copy fee. State law sets general clerk fees of $0.50 a page and $2 for the clerk's certificate, but whether Albemarle applies them to marriage records was not confirmed. The Office of Vital Records issues certified copies through its online system, by mail on Form VS6MD (a print-at-home PDF; include a legible copy of your ID), or at its Richmond lobby. Each certified copy, or a search when no copy is made, costs $15 (from July 1, 2026). Mailed requests are paid by check or money order payable to the State Health Department (the form says so); the page lists check, money order, payment card, mobile pay or cash only for applications dropped off at the lobby. VDH gives processing times of four weeks for mailed applications and two weeks for online ones. For 25 years after the marriage, Vital Records releases the record only to immediate family with valid ID. The DMV may also issue certified marriage records ($15 plus a $2 processing fee).
steps.fee: $15 for each certified copy, or a search when no copy is made, from the Office of Vital Records (DMV: $15 plus a $2 processing fee); the Albemarle Clerk's copy fee is not published
steps.quote: the $15.00 fee rate will apply to each certified copy of a vital record that is issued, or for each search of the system of vital records where a certified copy of a vital record is not made.

escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court (venue for mandamus lies where the record or proceeding is): a petition for a writ of mandamus, verified by oath and served with notice on the clerk a reasonable time before it is presented, asking the court to order the license issued

escalation.deadline: The clerk's list is due no later than March 31 each year, for licenses issued in the preceding calendar year

escalation.quote: In the event such officiant dies or becomes incapacitated before completing the certificate of marriage, the official who issued the marriage license shall complete the certificate of marriage upon the order of the court to which is submitted proof that the marriage was performed.

escalation.trigger: An error on the marriage record
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk: an application under oath with supporting evidence; the clerk may amend the record and sends a certified copy of the correction to the State Registrar

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The pages of albemarlemarriage.org, vacourts.gov, albemarleso.org and vdh.virginia.gov were read live. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

No Albemarle marriage-license information page was found. The Clerk's page and its subpages (current and back to the 2013 County site, which pointed to the vacourts.gov court page) publish no fee, ID rule, payment methods, appointment rule or rule on whether both people must be present. The steps therefore rest on state law, the vacourts.gov hours and the online application's welcome page. Confirm with the Clerk's Office at 434-972-4083 before you go.

albemarlemarriage.org: only its welcome page was read. Its 'Proceed to Application' button submits a form, so it was not used, and nothing was submitted. What the application asks, whether it is required or only saves time at the counter, how long entries are kept, and what happens next are not known. The site is not on albemarle.org, but the Clerk's official page links to it as 'Marriage License Application', and the page names the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk. The only archive copy is from 2021.

Whether both people must appear together is not stated for Albemarle. Va. Code § 20-16 requires the parties to state the information under oath; the Charlottesville Clerk requires both to be present at once, with a special process when one is incarcerated. No Albemarle or Code provision on remote or one-party applications was found.
ID: no Albemarle page and no Code section requiring photo ID was found; the advice to bring government photo ID is general practice at other Virginia clerks, not an Albemarle rule.

Fee: the $30 total is the sum of the state tax (§ 20-15) and the clerk's fee (§ 17.1-275(A)(5)). Albemarle publishes neither the amount it charges nor the payment methods it accepts. Some Virginia clerks charge more, for example to include a certified copy; whether Albemarle does is not known.

Appointments: the Clerk's page (2026-05-09 capture) has a 'We are closed to public traffic' link to the press release of January 6, 2021, but it sits inside an HTML comment, so the page does not display it; the Documents Center (2026-06-12 capture) still lists that release as 'Clerks Office COVID19 Order'. The release said 'Appointments for marriage licensing will be required' during COVID-19. That notice is very likely outdated: the County's June 2025 notice says the Clerk's Office opened to the public from 8 am to 4 pm in the new courthouse. Ask whether an appointment is needed. The 2021 notice also gives a mailing address (501 East Jefferson Street) that is not recorded here because it may be stale.

Location: the County announced on 2025-06-23 that the General District and Circuit Courts were moving to the new courthouse adjacent to Court Square, a 'permanent relocation of court operations to the new facility'. The County and vacourts.gov pages still give 350 Park Street, Court Square. The Courts Complex page (2026-04-12 capture) says a second phase will renovate and add to the historic courthouse for the Circuit Court, with completion expected in 2027, so the Clerk's counter may move within the complex. Confirm the entrance before visiting.

Security: the screening and phone rules come from the Albemarle County Sheriff's Office 'Core Responsibilities' page ('all persons and parcels entering the courts are subject to search', and cell phones and other electronic or recording devices 'are prohibited beyond the security screening desks at Albemarle County Circuit Court'). Whether the Clerk's Office counter is past the screening desks was not confirmed.

Officiant orders: the Albemarle Civil Division page links 'Petition to Perform One-Time Marriage Ceremony', a scanned two-page form (CC-1498 MASTER 07/18, a petition to the Court, and CC-1499 MASTER 07/18, an order signed by a judge). It has no text layer, so no quote is taken from it; its form fields (petitioner, case number, judge's signature line, bond penalty and surety) and its July 2018 scan date fit that description, but the printed form numbers are not confirmed. The Documents Center lists the same PDF as 'Perform Marriage Ceremony - Updated', and the Clerk's 'Forms for Various Circuit Court Filings' link redirects to the vacourts.gov civil forms page, which carries the current CC-1498. Current § 20-25 (as amended through 2026, c. 437) has the application filed with and the order issued by the clerk, and the current state form CC-1498 MASTER 07/26 is an application to the Clerk with a box to ask that no bond be required. Which version Albemarle accepts, how long it takes, whether the officiant must apply in their home circuit, and whether it can be filed by mail were not found.

No Albemarle source offering civil wedding ceremonies was found. The Albemarle Clerk's pages list no officiants, and the Albemarle County Sheriff's website (home page, core responsibilities and sitemap) does not mention weddings. Unlike the Charlottesville Sheriff, no Albemarle wedding service is recorded here.

Whether a refused applicant can get mandamus against the clerk is a legal judgment. Title 20 gives no appeal from a refusal; the only express fallback is the judge's power in § 20-14 when the clerk and deputies cannot act. The mandamus rungs rest on the general procedure in §§ 8.01-644 and 8.01-645, the venue rule in § 8.01-261(5) and on issuance being a clerk's duty under §§ 20-14 and 20-13.2. Applying to another circuit court clerk is the practical alternative. § 20-25 makes officiant orders discretionary ('may issue') and gives no appeal; it also makes the clerk immune from suit over issuing or rescinding them, absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.

No residency requirement: inferred from § 20-14 ('a circuit court of any county or city') and stated outright on the Charlottesville Clerk's page; Albemarle's pages do not address it. No Code section setting a waiting period or requiring a blood test was found; Albemarle's pages do not address them either.

No Albemarle County Code section governs marriage licenses; state law sets the requirements, fee and validity. The County Code is published on Municode, whose CivicPlus terms forbid automated access and copying, so it was not searched. The four local legal_basis entries are office procedures from the Clerk's online application page, the Clerk's Civil Division page and the vacourts.gov court page, not ordinances.

Copies from the Clerk: the Clerk's Office publishes no procedure or fee for copies of marriage records. Va. Code § 17.1-208(B) opens clerks' records to inspection and requires copies on request for a reasonable fee under § 17.1-275; §§ 17.1-275(A)(8) and (A)(9) set general fees of $0.50 a page and $2 for the clerk's certificate, but whether Albemarle applies them to marriage certificates was not confirmed. Applications and registers that show social security or control numbers are not open to general public inspection (§ 32.1-267(F)).

Vital Records: the $15 fee took effect on July 1, 2026 (VDH notice citing Chapter 616 of the 2026 Acts of Assembly); the index text of § 32.1-273 (cap of $15; history ending '2026, c. 616') matches. Because clerks forward marriage records to the State Registrar monthly (§ 32.1-267(D)), a state copy may not be available right after the wedding; that is an inference, not something either office states. The VS6MD PDF declares a form dictionary with an empty field list and no widgets, and VDH lists it among 'PDF forms to print at home', so it is recorded as not fillable.
The Albemarle Clerk's page warns: 'the clerk's office says the law bars it from giving legal advice.'

Privacy: the Clerk's County page names the Clerk and the Chief Deputy Clerk, and its 'Email the Department' link goes to the Clerk's personal mailbox; the Civil Division page names staff; the vacourts.gov page names the Clerk and the judges; the Courts Complex page names a project manager. None are recorded. No general office mailbox for the Clerk's Office was found, so no email contact is listed.

State-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia; some keep that copy's spacing before punctuation (for example '§ 20-25 , $25'). Section text has not been compared with the live law.lis.virginia.gov pages.
